objective: Eliminate overkill on trivial tasks WITHOUT bypassing high-risk gates. Fast path is an OPT-IN permission granted by the admission decision, never a default, never a risk bypass.

antiOverkillGuarantees: a one-line text edit does NOT spawn sub-agents, Colima, durable execution, or a review bundle
no isolation is started unless a trigger demands it
no persistent state is created for a stateless task
no large review bundle for a trivial task
no repair graph for a task with repair_budget 0
guardrails: size/risk classification runs the SAME deterministic classifier — a trivial-looking but risky task lands in the HIGH/CRITICAL profile, not the fast path
fast path decisions are still recorded as a machine-readable admission result (schema-compliant, evidence_level none)
any single HIGH-class signal anywhere in the task text forces escalation (fail-closed) — the classifier scans the FULL task statement, not just a summary
fast path evidence: the admission record + the final diff + a minimal run event (telemetry), nothing more
controller/card may always opt OUT of the fast path (fast path is a permission, not a mandate)
fast path NEVER performs: memory write-back, commit/push/merge/release/seal, network writes, production runtime changes — those signals are definitionally non-LOW

steps: 1. admission classifies (XS|S, LOW, evidence sufficient) -> profile FAST_PATH
2. direct in-place execution by the executor (no sub-agent graph, no Colima, no worktree)
4. evidence_level none: admission record + diff + minimal telemetry event
5. no review bundle, no external review, no closeout state (unless lifecycle authority demands it)
6. result recorded; if any runtime anomaly contradicts the LOW classification -> stop and escalate (HOLD), never continue on the fast path

exampleAntiOverkill.task: fix a typo in a README sentence
exampleAntiOverkill.whySafe: no signals; reversible; no tests; single file
exampleAntiOverkill.whyNotBypassed: the same classifier escalates any destructive or secret-adjacent wording to at least HIGH even if the diff looks trivial
